This is an appeal filed by appellant under section 14-A(2) of Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 for grant of bail in connection with Crime No.104/2024 registered at Police Station Nagjhiri, District Ujjain (MP) for offence under Sections 376, 323, 294,
506, 190, 34 of Indian Penal Code, 1860 and also under Sections 3(1)(Wii), 3(2)(Va), 3(2)(v) of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 and Sections 4,5 of Traffic Prevention Act.

T his appeal under Section 14(A)(2) of the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 has been filed against order dated 27.7.2024 passed by Special Judge [under SC/ST(PA) Act] Ujjain whereby Vishakha vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 14 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195575555/

sentences.text:
She is in detention since 25.4.2024.
3 .
The allegation against the appellant is that she along with other co- accused persons has made contact of the prosecutrix with the main accused persons Shubham and Aman.
4 . Learned counsel for the appellant has submitted that appellant is innocent and has not committed any offence.
The prosecutrix is a major lady.
The main allegation of rape is against Shubham and Aman.
The FIR was lodged after four days of the incident and no satisfactory reasons has been assigned by the prosecution in this regard.
The appellant is having no previous criminal record.
The appellant being a lady, is in jail since 24.4.2024 and final conclusion of trial will take sufficient long time.
Therefore, it has been prayed that the appellant/accused be released on bail.
5 . O n the other hand, learned counsel for the State has opposed the prayer made by the counsel for the appellant but has fairly admitted that the appellant is having no criminal records.

6. Having taken into consideration all the facts and circumstances of the case and custody period of the appellant as well as nature of allegation but without expressing any opinion on the merit of the case, I am of the view that it is a fit case for grant of bail.
Consequently, appeal stands allowed.

7. It is directed that appellant be released on bail on her furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for her regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that she shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it during trial.

She shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 437(3) of Cr.P.C.
8.
This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case o f bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
Certified copy as per rules.
